utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The affirmation you made to tell the truth at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zyrapi. I want to --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you one last document relating to the topic of orders which we couldn't finish yesterday, and this is 65 ter number 4301. We see here it's a document from the 10th of January, 1999, and I'm interested in the first paragraph above the name -- the word "order." And it says here in the last lines of that paragraph: "The General Staff at its meeting of 5 January 1999 issued the following order ..." Could you tell me, were you participating in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And -- please --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was. This was the meeting of zone commanders that was held in the General Staff and order was issued from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where exactly was that meeting, in what location?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting was held in Divjak, where the General Staff was based.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who issued the order which is referred to here at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was issued by the Operational Zone of Pashtrik. The signature is not of the zone commander but the deputy zone commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we scroll down that the witness is seeing the signature, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What's the name of the deputy zone commander?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the commander is Ekrem Rexha, but as you can see from the signature it was signed by Kolcaku.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I -- we misunderstood each other. I wanted to know who at the General Staff meeting issued the order which prompted the order of the deputy commander from the operational zone.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order of the staff was issued by me, and it is related to transportation issues. The zones could use vehicles that they needed especially in various terrain, rough terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I, with this explanation, seek to tender this document which has the 65 ter number 4301, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00440, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on to my next topic, discipline within the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can we have 65 ter 2448 being shown to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here from the handwritten date it is from the 28th of November, 1998, and my first question is: Who signed that order?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we go to number 3 of your order we see here: "Improper behaviour with respect to the civilian population is to be prevented in all KLA units." Could you tell me what it was that prompted you to write such an order?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I issued the order after I had contacts with the zone commanders, and I heard complaints by superior officers that units from one zone went to another zone and had improper behaviour towards the population, had taken equipment from them without issuing the appropriate documentation; and that's what prompted me to issue this order for the KLA soldiers and their way of behaviour towards the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So the units who took items from the civilian populations were KLA units or elements thereof, better said?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what improvement, if any, followed that order of yours?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the order was issued, the behaviour of members of the KLA improved considerably.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I seek to tender 2448, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00441, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document has a 65 ter number 2463.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We stay in the area of discipline. We see here that the first line tells us: "Pursuant to an Order by the Investigate Judge ..." and the order is 10 February 1999, Mr. Ekrem Rexha issues this order. Could you first of all tell me, had the investigative judge in 1999 the authority to issue an order to zone commander of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To whom -- or who was the superior of such an investigative judge, if there was any?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time the head of the military court was Sokol Dobruna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And on what level was Sokol Dobruna working, at what level within the KLA structure?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sokol Dobruna was above the general Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So to clarify, he was a member of the General Staff of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation could I seek to tender document 2463, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, Mr. Zyrapi, what was the request of the investigating judge that's referred to in paragraph 1 of the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember this case; however, it says here that the investigating judge had given an order, maybe a disciplinary issue had arisen, and the military police of the zone is placed at the disposal of carrying out this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do I understand from that that the investigating judge could not himself make a binding order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The investigating judge had issued an order about an investigation, but this order had to go through the commander of the operational zone in order to be executed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00442, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document has 65 ter number 2464.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we see it's a document dated from the 1st of February, 1999, from the Operation Zone Pashtrik. Could you tell me - and I'm reading here from the paragraph above order, the word "order," it says on the basis of certain articles of the disciplinary regulations of the General Staff of the KLA. What are these disciplinary regulations?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about this yesterday. We had the interim regulations of the KLA which was amended and completed with other rules as the time went by. The articles of these regulations were used to take disciplinary measures against the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if I look here at number 1 of that order it says that a man, Hasan O Bej has to be in the detention for the period of 48 hours. If you remember that case, what conduct of Mr. Bej prompted that he had to go for two days into detention?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it a little bit. I think he misused his weapon. He used his weapon to fire in the air. That's why the disciplinary measure was taken against him for this offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you explain to us, we see that Mr. Ekrem Rexha, the commander of the Pashtrik zone, is issuing that order. Had a zone commander in the KLA disciplinary powers so that he himself without a judge could issue such an order?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he could issue orders. They -- there were also legal advisors working with the commander, the zone commander, who could advise them about disciplinary measures of this sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I tender 2464, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00443, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document is 4300, 65 ter number 4300.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we see here in front of us, it's an order from the 18th of January, 1999, again from the Operation Zone Pashtrik. And I'm just summarising briefly paragraphs 1 and 2 of that order. A state of military-readiness is declared here. And number 2 says: "All officers and soldiers" of that zone "who are outside their unit should report immediately to" the "base in the Operational Zone Pashtrik." And I'm only interested now in number 7 of that order, and it says in English: "Disrespect for this order will result in penal discipline, whereby immediate and rigorous measures will be taken." Could you explain what disciplinary measures, if any, were envisaged in case the soldiers who were ordered here did not report back to their duty?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, if the soldiers did not comply with the order, they would be declared deserters and the military court would be used to take measures against the soldier or superior officer who did not report. We used for this the former laws used in the Yugoslav Army as well as international laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation can I tender 65 ter 4300 into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00444, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The last document on discipline has the 65 ter number 4183. While this is being shown, can we also have the map from yesterday, which I did not tender -- oh, it's lying already next to the witness on the ELMO. That's, for the record, 65 ter number 615.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is a document here from the Serb side from the 11th of January, 1999, from the state security RDB of the Ministry of Interior, and I don't want to delve into the formalities of the document, just ask you to look into the first paragraph where it is mentioned in the second line, talking about the territory of Suva Reka municipality, that the main stronghold is in Brezance village, the site of the KLA Main Staff for that municipality. Could you, by looking on the map next to you, encircle for us where that Brezance village is which is talked about here in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I see the ELMO appears or I don't get an image of the ELMO here on my screen. Thank you. We would need to zoom out a little bit, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a topographic map and this village is a very small one, that's why it's not on the map, but it's approximately here where I made this circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And for the record you have marked a number 4 next to the circle where you believe that Brezance is. Going back now to the document which talks about that village, it says that an army barracks is in that village. Which unit was located in Brezance village, which KLA unit?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 123rd Brigade which was located in this village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then we see in the same sentence it talks, next to a military hospital, about a prison which was formed. Can you explain, if you know, what that reference may mean.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each brigade command had a room for keeping in isolation or for detaining the people who violated the rules. There was a hospital that was located in Pagarusha.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark, if it is visible on the map, where that place, Pagarusha, is by encircling it and marking a 5 next to it.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. We were now talking about the 123rd Brigade. Can you tell me in general did KLA brigades have some detention rooms, or was it only in the case of the 123rd KLA Brigade that such detention rooms would exist?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other brigades had them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What about operational zones, did they have detention rooms?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on to my next topic which is territory held or controlled by the KLA. If we stay in this document for a second, and I'm referring to the first sentence here. The Serbian State Security Service reports here on the 11th of January, 1999, and I'm reading the first sentence that: "In the territory of Suva Reka municipality, most villages are controlled by the terrorists of the so-called KLA." Could you, being the Chief of Staff of the KLA at the time, comment upon that assessment from the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that most of the villages in Suhareke municipality were under the control of 123rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I understand here the reference, it talks about the territory of Suva Reka municipality. Could you clarify whether the entire municipality was the A OR of the 123rd Brigade or of several other brigades?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the villages, as I said, were under the command or control of the 123rd Brigade. It is possible that a village belonged to the area of responsibility of another brigade, depending on the border separating two neighbouring brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just asking because -- were other KLA brigades in the territory of Suva Reka municipality at the time, on 11th of January, also controlling territory of Suva Reka municipality, as the Serb side alleges?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the northern part of Suhareke, some villages were under or in the area of responsibility of 121 Brigade, whereas the remaining villages were under the control of 123rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation could I seek to tender 65 ter number 4183, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00445, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you now 65 ter number 2460, a document from the KLA side roughly in the same time-period. We see it's the 28th of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we could just for a second move to the signature on the last side, and we only need to do that in the Albanian version. I want the witness to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We could now go to page 3 -- yeah, to page 3 in both versions, and I'm interested in the letter (g) which says "our forces" -- "combat situation," and then there is a subheading "our forces." And in the B/C/S we would need -- I think the witness has read the last two lines. We would need to switch to the next page as well. So that the witness can read the next page because it goes onto the next page -- in Albanian we need to go to the next page I wanted to say, to page number 4, please, and there the upper part, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, if you read this briefly, it says in your document - and this is in English somewhere in the middle - it says: " ... we can freely say," I quote, "that the territory controlled by our units is now of a greater percentage than prior to the enemy offensive." What I'm interested in is: Which enemy offensive were you referring to here, and when was that offensive coming to an end?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the offensive launched by the Serb military and police forces. It commenced in July and finished sometime in October 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do I interpret your sentence correctly that following the end of that offensive in October 1998, as you just explained, the territory controlled by our units is now of a greater percentage, territory controlled by whom?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Our units" means KLA units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you tell me why was, in your assessment, by December, end of December 1998, the KLA holding a greater percentage of territory?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this offensive, the KLA units withdrew during this offensive and had smaller territories; but after the offensive itself the units consolidated, the number of soldiers increased, and they spread their territory that was under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And before in the document we were talking about Suva Reka municipality. In this document about which parts of Kosovo are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document does not refer only to the Suhareke territory, but also to the Dukagjini territory based on the report that was compiled by the commander of the zone at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I seek to tender 65 ter number 2460 into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00446, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document is 4186.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here it's from the 13th of March, 1999, a document a few days before the NATO air-strikes begin. And it is again from the state security department of the MUP, so from, if I may call it, the other side. And I'm interested in page 5 of that document in both versions. There is a headline entitled "Prizren Municipality." If you would please read the first paragraph. It will be enlarged shortly. We see here in the first paragraph mentioning is made of the villages of Pirane and Randobrava. If you look at the map next to you, could you first of all point -- not encircle, just point with a marker for Your Honours' benefit where Pirane and Randobrava are located. No need to mark it. Just point at it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The ELMO needs to be moved, Your Honours, or the -- could we zoom out a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah. Can you just for Your Honours' benefit point -- yes, yeah, you have marked a dot for Your Honours' benefit where Pirane and Randobrava are. Thank you. And moving on in the document we have seen which the occasion is which are referred to here in the document. We see that 50 to 70 terrorists are mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that the witness did not mark Randobrava and Mr. Neuner has just indicated that he did. Pirane, yes, but Randobrava, no, as far as I can see. I don't know if you are seeing the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He marked two towns, one almost directly north of the other, two villages, and they are both Randobrava and Pirane.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah, I wanted to move on in the document itself. If we move on, we have clarified what the area is, to the next paragraph, it is mentioned here about the terrorists, so to speak. And I'm quoting: "They have built fortifications and bunkers and set up a check-point with armed men on the hill between Randobrava and Mala Krusa, overlooking Mala Krusa close to the Kosovo Vine cellars ..." Could you, if we talk about this check-point on the hill, indicate for Your Honours where that check-point on the hill is.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a hill above Randobrava, or rather, between Randobrava and Krusha e Vogel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark on your map by encircling this time where you believe that check-point on the hill is.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe number 6 is the next highest number we would need.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, did you ever visit that spot which you have encircled as number 6?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During February/March time-period, I toured not only this check-point but more or less the entire defence line. It was like an observation post that observed the movement along Prizren-Gjakove main road. So this was the movement from Prizren direction towards Gjakove covering also Xerxe and the bridge of Rashevc [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I listened carefully to what you just explained. You are referring to this spot which you have marked as number 6 as an observation point, while the Serb side here says it was a check-point which indicates to me that there were cars controlled. Can you explain to me what you believed when you were there, what activity was going on on that hill from the KLA side?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a point in the defence line of the KLA, and as I said earlier, it was an observation post like an observation of the terrain was carried out from that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If cars passed through, were they stopped and controlled and checked?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cars could not pass through this area. It was a hilly part, so it was just part of the defence line of the KLA, this check-point from where we carried out the observation of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now I hear in the translation it was a check-point. I'm just trying to clarify. The Serb side says it was a check-point and you used a couple of times observation point. Could you just clarify one last time what that spot was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we have it clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have it clarified. Okay. Then I would seek to tender that document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00447, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document is 2462.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see it's a document from the 125th Brigade, and I'm interested in the -- in Albanian the third-last paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could scroll down a little bit for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- and in English the fourth-last paragraph starting with: "On Thursday, the 25th of March ..." And I'm quoting here: "On Thursday, 25th of March, 1999, the first Serb offensive of this year began all of over Kosovo by stretching to include Prizren and Rahovec municipalities. Krusha e Madhe and Krusha e Vogel suffered most, as did the surrounding villages." Could you by looking at the map next to you encircle, first of all, Krusha e Vogel.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And mark a number 7.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm then continuing in the text: "Serb forces stretched to include the villages of Pirane-Zejz and Mrovec."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as Krusha e Vogel is concerned, on the map that I have it's -- it was marked yesterday. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can explain that yesterday I had him mark the train station of Krusha e Vogel, and today I had marked him Krusha e Vogel proper, which is the village itself. I can ask the witness to clarify if this is a concern of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I say, Mr. Neuner, that the map shows in the grey shaded area the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the circle of the witness with number 1 encircles the grey shaded area of the village. It may also contain the railway station, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will clarify, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I really wonder that you need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Then I leave it here. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the text briefly it says in the next sentence: "On this very day," referring to the 25th of March, "the village population left and sheltered in the village of Mamusha." Could you please show by encircling, Your Honours -- by encircling on the map, could you show Your Honours where Mamusha is.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And mark an 8 next to it.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And my last question relating to this document relates to Friday, the 26th, it's two paragraphs down there in the text. "On Friday, the 26th of March ..." and I'm leaving out a passage, "around 1720 the village was surrounded by numerous Serbian forces that took their positions with tanks, armoured vehicles, and heavy machine-guns in the woods ..." Could you tell me, you were the Chief of Staff of the KLA at the time, have you heard that the Serb forces were deploying tanks on Friday, the 26th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had this as an information from the reports received from the zone commander, brigade commander. I was informed that that the Serb forces launched their attack earlier, on the 25th, and advanced further in the territory of the 124 and 125 Brigade. So I have received this information on the movement of armed -- armoured personnel carriers and tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you by looking at the map next to you draw, so to speak, if you know, an arrow indicating the beginning and the direction of movement of the tanks?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the report I received from the commander at the time, the armoured military vehicles moved along this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You have drawn three arrows. How did you react to that information?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon receiving the information, the first order was for the units to withdraw to the second and third line of defence in order to consolidate the defence, and all units that had equipment, antitank equipment, had an order to use them in order to repel the attack or the offensive of the enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where were you going, if anywhere, upon receiving that information?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness did not say where he was when he received the information. He merely stated that he received the information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where were you when you received that information?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Divjake, in the General Staff building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did you stay all the time in the General Staff building in Divjak or did you move somewhere; if so, where?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I moved depending on the intensity of fighting at the time. So as Serb forces advanced in this direction, I moved to the zone command based at Nishor; and together with zone command, we went on the ground to organise a defence line at Dobrodolan village where there were units that had previously withdrawn from the defence line, units that belonged to the 124 and 125 Brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you briefly mark, if it's on the map, Dobrodolan. Encircle it and mark a 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then I would seek to tender that map, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 615.06.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00448, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move quickly to the map which you gave in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was just informed that the document which I had shown to the witness was not tendered yet. I would seek to tender also the document 2462. That's the 65 ter number into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That too will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00449, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the map can be removed from the witness -- from the ELMO I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Interpretation] Your Honour, could you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That couldn't be heard, I'm afraid, by the interpreter, Mr. Djurdjic. Could you repeat what you've said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there was only the first page of this document that has been admitted was shown on the screen. We could only see the heading. We didn't see the end of the document, whether it was signed, by whom, and whether this is an authentic document, whether that can be verified. That's why I'm asking why only the page that we see on the screen is admitted or is the document in its entirety admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document has been tendered in its entirety. If you think there is a dispute about its authenticity, you may pursue that in cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe before the document disappears from the screen or it's already disappeared --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, the document you have just seen last, who produced that document to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, together with other documents, were produced by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did you obtain that document before you brought it to us?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I obtained it from the archives of the Pashtrik Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I forgot now, Your Honours, did it receive already an -- it did already receive an exhibit number. I want to move on to the next document which is Exhibit 427, and I would also need the last page. This is, for Your Honours' information, the witness statement which I tendered yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We were just discussing about the operation near Pirane-Mala Krusa, and the next map was attached here to your witness statement. I would be interested once it comes up if you tell us who has produced it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We can go in one-screen mode, for the usher's assistance, because this is a very huge map. And if we could focus simply on the lower markings, it's roughly in the middle of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, because you see the map already, who has produced this map?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I produced the map, and I made the lines and the drawings on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we now zoom in very much on the letter A which we see in the middle right now on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah, could you -- just that we orientate ourselves - tell us, is the area around letter A almost similar to the area of the map which we just saw where you made all these nine to ten markings?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately; however, this map contains more detail about villages, but it's the same part of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm leading the witness a little bit. I just wanted to have a few explanations for Your Honours' benefit. I note also the time. I'm almost winding down, Your Honours. I just -- I'm leading at this point in time just to explain you the background of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell us by drawing a long arrow, if you can, in which direction the Serb forces, which we understood were coming from the western side, in which direction were the Serb forces moving at the end of March 1999?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is all in evidence, my learned colleague. I'm just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you address the Chamber, not other counsel, Mr. Neuner. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, the witness never said that Serb forces were coming from the west, not at any point. Second, I wonder whether this document has been tendered into evidence or not, although I can take care of that later on during my cross. But any mention of the west relating to the axis of movement of the Serb forces was never made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe that is correct, Mr. Neuner. And this map has not been tendered as an exhibit, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am told, Mr. Djurdjic, that this map is, in fact, the last page of Exhibit P427, the statement of the witness, so it is part of Exhibit P427. Now, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, it is tendered already. I just wanted to highlight a few portions for Your Honours' benefit. The entire operation which is ensuing has been discussed at length in the witness's last testimony in the Milutinovic et al case, and I'm talking about 5.900 -- transcript pages 5.990 till 6.008. I'm just trying to show Your Honours briefly the introduction to that map, what the background is. And I didn't want to spend much time on this. I see I'm getting objections, but everything, I believe, is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you - and I'm withdrawing my earlier question - just indicate from which side to which side the Serb forces were moving? You can draw over that map an arrow to indicate the direction of movement of the Serb forces on the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I can recall, reading the transcript from the Milutinovic case, I think that the witness then marked in red ink the positions and activities of the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There is a red marking on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm asking -- which are multiple markings. I'm just asking about the general direction of the movement of the Serb forces and that is all. While the witness has marked some individual red markings which is all explained already. I just wanted Your Honours to grasp in which direction the Serb forces overall were moving throughout the operation, and the witness has now marked, for the record, an arrow indicating the direction of overall movement. And maybe with that explanation I would just seek to tender this one page because I wanted to move inside the map to other areas. Could I seek to tender just this one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00450, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we, by zooming in on the map again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the version of the map that the witness has just marked has now been zoomed in, and it is only a portion of the earlier map; in other words, the other map contained other portions as well that were marked in phases, I think A, B, C, and D. I think that's how the witness marked them. So that now we have a confusion here because we just see a section of this map without actually being able to see the rest of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- the entire map is in evidence, Your Honours. The problem of that map is it's of a very small scale, and if one prints it out, it is almost -- since it is so small it is almost hard to catch with the own eye. What I'm just doing is I'm blowing up portions here of the map to make it more legible and understandable. We can have one general explanation per A, B, C, D, which is marked here on these maps, tender them in a larger scale so that Your Honours can make sense out of it. That's all I'm doing. I thought I'm sitting in a few minutes' time, but I'm getting very many objections about that. The entire map as such is in evidence and Your Honours can look at it, but as I believe, it is very difficult to understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could now ask the usher to pull us the other section of this overall map relating to B, C, and D. Just -- I need this portion so it's more visible for Your Honours. We don't need A any longer. Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here B and C and front of us. You have already marked for us the lower part. Could you just explain to us where was the offensive -- the Serb offensive, if at all, proceeding, just by indicating a rough arrow?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it continued to the territory of Pagarusha --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, we have lost --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and towards --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have we still kept the marking of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We need to start afresh, Witness. Could you please mark again.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it started in Dobrodolan, towards Pagarusha, and further on to Berisha, where it stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark roughly the line where the Serb offensive stopped?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have drawn an arrow indicating the direction of movement, first of all, as explanation for the record.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was there at the time, it is about here that the offensive stopped. The Serb forces did not continue further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have marked a dotted line where you believe that the Serb forces stopped. Around what time did the Serb forces stop in 1999 at this line?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was about the 26th and the 27th of March. There were sporadic fightings on the other days as well, but the Serb forces did not go beyond this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you just encircle where the headquarter of the General Staff of the KLA was at the time for Your Honours' attention.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And mark a 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would seek to tender that annotated map into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00451, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The last document I have for you has exhibit number -- 65 ter number 2457. 65 ter number is 2457. And my first question is: Who signed that order?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was signed by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you're ordering here the Pashtrik Operational Zone to establish a defence line, and that's on the 1st of April, 1999. Could you explain whether this defence line was indeed established.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This defence line, although the order was given, was not established -- or they started to establish it, but because of the Serb offensive they had to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I nevertheless with that explanation seek to tender that document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00452, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have just seen here that you're trying through such orders to create defence lines against the Serb -- advancing Serb forces. Could you tell me, Did the General Staff of the KLA in March/April 1999 have some own forces at their disposal which could be used to reinforce zone commanders' troops?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time the General Staff had units at its disposal, also units of the military police, the intelligence unit, and sabotage unit. These were used to reinforce the troops in the zones according to their demands or requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So how many troops did the General Staff itself command, how many men, how many soldiers, in March/April 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were about 300 soldiers of the KLA assigned to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Neuner. It's probably convenient, is it, Mr. Djurdjic, to have the break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think it would be preferable to take the break now so that I can prepare and then we can be more efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will need to have a break now to resume at ten minutes to 11.00, half an hour. We adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Djurdjic has some questions for you now, Mr. Zyrapi. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examination by Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zyrapi, my name is Veljko Djurdjic. And I am a member of the Defence team of the accused, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic. With me today is Ms. Marie O'Leary, a member of our team. Would you please listen carefully to my questions and answer my questions specifically so that we can complete the cross-examination as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have Exhibit P00436 on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the next page where the actual text begins.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, these are the interim regulations on the organisation of internal affairs in the army that you mentioned yesterday. Would you please read the military declaration, the contents of the military oath, which is under Roman II, subparagraph 1. Could you please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "As a member of the Kosovo Liberation Army, I hereby swear that I will fight for the liberation of the occupied territories of Albania and their unification, that I will always be a loyal soldier, a worthy soldier of freedom, vigilant, brave, and disciplined, ready at all times, even unto death to struggle to protect the sacred interests of the Fatherland. If I break this oath, may I be punished by the most severe martial law and if I commit treason may my blood be spent. I swear!"

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi. This is an oath that each new member of the KLA had to make; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the oath that was taken in the beginning, but it changed in the later period.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. This oath states that: "I shall fight for the liberation of the occupied territories of Albania and their unification." Could you please explain to us what occupied territories of Albania is this a reference to and what are the territories that are supposed to be unified?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This oath that was taken at the time comprised Kosova, part of Macedonia, part of Serbia, and part of Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what did they mean by unification of all Albanian territories?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is about the unification of those territories that I mentioned together with Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please read Chapter II, Roman I, item 1, the national flag. This is on page 3 in Albanian and on the second page of the English version.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it now, yes. The raising of the national flag, meaning the red flag with the black eagle in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And this is the symbol of the state of all Albanians, if I'm not mistaken, that's what is stated here.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the national flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, in this document in chapter 7 on page 16 in Albanian and page 10 in English, it is stated: "All KLA activities have been stated in the platform of the Kosovo -- Albanian National Movement and in the platform of the Kosovo Liberation Army for liberation on unity." Mr. Zyrapi, could you tell us, please, what the Albanian National Movement is.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The creation of the KLA, its political base or foundation was the LPK, the patriotic movement of Kosova; and according to its platform, the KLA began to be formed based on the platform of the LPK.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I correct in saying that the KLA platform that was adopted was to separate the territories of Serbia, Macedonia, and Montenegro by force and -- and to annex them to the state of Albania, thus forming a greater Albanian state?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning the platform of the LPK was this, that you just read; however, the platform later on was changed so this platform was revised to the effect of liberation of the territory of Kosova and its secession from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi, but these were interim regulations on the organisation of internal affairs in the army that you passed in November -- in November 1998; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In November I received this document, the document was compiled earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, I've carefully read all your statements, but I must say that I am not clear on the structure and organisation of the Main Staff of the KLA. Could you please tell me in detail who was at the head of the Main Staff of the Kosovo Liberation Army. First could you just mention what the function was, the highest function.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the period November and onwards. There was a commander of the General Staff, deputy commanders of the General Staff, then there were the different departments of the directorate -- directorates of the staff and the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise, I was referring to the time when you were appointed as chief of the Main Staff. Could you please tell me, the commander of the Main Staff, who was it at this time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time commander of the chief -- the General Staff until March 1999 was Azem Syla.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And after March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After March until May commander of General Staff was Sylejman Selimi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say as of March, does this imply the time before the NATO operations or after the NATO operations?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was the deputy commander of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two deputy commanders of General Staff. One of them, Sokol Bashota, deputy commander for operations, whereas Jakup Krasniqi was the deputy commander of the General Staff for political issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. How many administrations did the General Staff of the Kosovo Liberation Army have?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially there were six, then the number of directorates increased depending on the needs, and to what I remember I think there were eight altogether later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I've reviewed many documents, but I never saw a document depicting the structure and organisation of the staff of the KLA. Does such a document exist?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement I did explain the commanding structure of the staff from top to bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi, but that was not my question. I did not ask of you to describe the structure and organisation, but rather, which document actually sets forth that organisation structure?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time there was, and this document was in the hands or with the commander of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And where is this document now, and when was it passed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it should be in the archives of the KLA, the adopted document; however, it was revised and changed. For the structure I'm talking about it referred to the period November and December 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were the Chief of Staff of the General Staff, were you in contact with other armies?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From November until April, I did not have contacts with other armies except with the KLA army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you have any contact with the NATO forces?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I did not mean you personally, but rather your General Staff, whether your General Staff had any relations or any contact with the NATO forces; and if so, what kind of relationship did they have?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time I was Chief of Staff, I did not have any knowledge of contacts between the KLA General Staff and NATO forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me try to refresh your memory, Mr. Zyrapi. You gave an interview to the Zeri newspaper and in answer to the question: During the air-strikes of NATO, the communication between the KLA and the NATO enabled the discovery of the military potentials of the Serb army and their front line, and in answer whether there were any other forms of cooperation with them you answered: During the air-strikes this was one of the main purpose of our cooperation, the coordination between the NATO and our own forces. Do you remember that you've said this?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the operations centre that informed on the groupings and movements of the Serb forces to inform the NATO forces that at the time were based in Macedonia and in Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please describe how you maintained communications between the operations centre of the Main Staff of the KLA and the NATO forces in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations department -- there was another part of the operations centre organised in Albania where the information on the movement and grouping of Serb forces were sent; and from there, the information was then conveyed to NATO forces, both in Albania and in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that at the time when you were appointed the Chief of the General Staff of the KLA, an agreement was signed, the Geremek-Jovanovic, Milosevic-Holbrooke and other agreements actually, and that those agreements established the Kosovo Verification Mission?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like us to get on our screens the Prosecution Exhibit P446. Mr. Zyrapi, this exhibit was admitted into evidence yesterday. You are familiar with it; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you signed it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm interested in this document -- well, the date is the 28th of December, 1998, and in paragraph (b) the last sentence reads: "The enemy suffered considerable losses in personnel and equipment with minimal consequences for our KLA units."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The counsel is kindly requested to slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us what you meant when you said that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report extracting from the report sent by zone commanders, a first report compiled during the meetings between the zone commanders and the General Staff, during which the zone commanders reported to the General Staff about the situation in their respective zones. So they reported on the damages inflicted on the Serb forces and on the KLA side for the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. This document was adopted by the KLA General Staff before you drafted it and submitted it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a report based on the reports received from the zone commanders. It was compiled, it was signed by me, and it was sent to the commander of the General Staff; and at the time it was the deputy commander of the General Staff who received the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph (d), the second-to-last sentence reads: "The Llap Operational Zone is different from other operational zones because it organised the Territorial Defence and civilian protection." Mr. Zyrapi, could you explain to me this Lap zone, what was this Territorial Defence and the civilian protection like, what did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Llapi Operational Zone, in addition to the regular KLA units, there were also civil protection units in order to secure the area, in order to help the population to evacuate in cases of fighting occurring in the areas where they lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And were those units different from the KLA units?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were different from the KLA units, both in terms of organisation, weapons, and leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. The General Staff, was it superior also to those units?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the Territorial Defence units and the civil protection units reported to the operational zone command and through that to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph (g) you say - and this was quoted back to you today - "After the enemy offensive, the forces were regrouped in the axis in all operational zones in positions there, and we can say that the territory controlled by our units is greater now than it was before the enemy offensive in percentage terms."

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that time, according to the report and after the offensive, I explained this earlier -- before the offensive, the KLA was covering smaller territories; however, later on the KLA developed gradually but it did not reach to the main roads and axis. However, the KLA developed in the villages and by that I mean the increase in number of soldiers and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just waited for the witness to finish because the question was not recorded. If you could just repeat your question, I think that's probably a possible course of action. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, your question came too quickly to be recorded, I believe, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So the response to my question before the intervention by my learned colleague, Mr. Neuner, was that -- well, the question was: Does that mean that you used the agreement that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia signed with the international officials to take territory that was now greater than it had been before the summer conflicts? Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, as the Chief of Staff you were quite aware of the fact that the agreement between the FRY and the international officials, all kinds of them, that it envisaged cessation of hostilities, a cease-fire; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the next sentence you say: "Special approach was taken by organising KLA units in towns and areas that were not under the control of the regular KLA units." Mr. Zyrapi, does that mean that in all towns in Kosovo you had your units set up?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because it wasn't possible to create the units in towns. The units were only in the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. But, Mr. Zyrapi, let me repeat: "Special approach was taken by organising KLA units in towns and areas that are not under the control of the regular units."

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe there is a mistake here made in the writing of the report; however, as I said earlier, there were no units in the towns because it was not possible to form that at that time. But there were units in the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, can you tell me what document actually served as a basis for the foundation of the military court of the Kosovo Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military court was formed at the same time that the General Staff was restructured. I'm speaking about the period when I was Chief of General Staff, so it coincided with the same period that the General Staff was restructured.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what document actually was used as a basis for the organisation of the military court?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier that the document used or documents used for the functioning of the military court were the former laws of the Army of Yugoslavia and international conventions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, you're not now telling us what regulations the military court applied, and I'm asking you how and when the military court was established, what was the founding document, the statute?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is the same document that established the restructuring of the General Staff. This was compiled in January/February. I was not Chief of Staff at the time, but I know that they worked with that document before I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. But you didn't tell me January, February -- what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi, but you were the Chief of the General Staff at that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from November, December, January, February, March, April.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter notes that it was the interpreter's mistake. The witness said: I was not present when the document was compiled, and not I was not Chief of Staff when the document was compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. But you must have seen this document?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document for the restructuring of the General Staff was the same document that founded the military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And until now this document has not been seen or shown in this court. Have you seen it yourself?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, because on the basis of that document, the staff was organised and restructured. But the after the air-strikes and the offensives, the documents were transported and moved elsewhere, and not everything was taken away with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me based on this document that you had seen how the judiciary was set up in the KLA, the judicial organs?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it envisaged the creation of the military court. At the General Staff each zone command would have a legal advisor, and this was also sent to the brigades. This would be the structure of the military court at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't know if I understood you correctly. Today you said that the president of the court was a member of the General Staff of the Kosovo Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was member of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you tell me what judges were appointed to this court which was attached to the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sokol Dobruna was head of the military court, and he was also part of the General Staff. And he reported to the general commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. That means that he was the only judge; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were others as well, but I don't remember them because I did not have contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. But where was the seat of the court?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sokol Dobruna was located in the Berisha mountains, first in Divjake for a short period of time, and then he moved to Novoselle or Shati i Ri.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know of any cases that were tried until its completion before the military court?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I know that there were cases, but I can't remember exactly which ones they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, you told us yesterday that when you were appointed the Chief of the General Staff, operational zones were set up, seven of them; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the usher to put on our screens a Defence document, that's D002-4026. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now here where we see Glogovac and Srbica --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely, if you could zoom in on that area. Could you scroll down a little bit. Yes, yes, just, or rather, scroll up. No, you were heading in the right direction. Could you scroll down a little bit so that Srbica or Skenderaj is moving towards the top of the screen. A little bit more. A little bit more. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please mark the Drenica Operational Zone here on this map.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will start from here because the map does not go further down enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the usher to zoom out because the witness can't now draw in the entire zone -- it's impossible to do it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We lose what's there if it's altered now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, sir, could you please tell me where was the headquarters of the Drenica Operational Zone when you were appointed the Chief of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The headquarters of the Drenica Operational Zone was based at Likoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me who was the commander of the Drenica Operational Zone while you were the Chief of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until March 1999, the Drenica commander was Sylejman Selimi. From March onwards, the commander was Sami Lushtaku.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me, the General Staff when you were appointed its head, was it located in the Drenica Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was appointed Chief of Staff of the General Staff of the KLA, the General Staff was not based there. Part of the General Staff that was in Kosova was in Shati i Ri in the Berisha mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I did not quite understand where the Berisha mountains are. Could you please tell me exactly so I can have a clear understanding.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They start here between the municipalities of Gllogoc, Malisheve, Shtime, Lipjan, so it goes from the Llapushnik gorge up to Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please mark Likoc with a number 1 so that we know that this is where the Main Staff of the operative zone was?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me, what brigades were within the operational zone of Drenica in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999 the brigades were 111th, 112th, 113th, and 114th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please tell me, where was the 111th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time the 111th Brigade was partly based in Likoc, another part of it was in the surrounding villages. I can't remember exactly where. This brigade was a rapid intervention brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now draw a wider circle around Likoc to depict where the 111th Brigade was and then please mark that with 111 on the outside of the circle.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. If I understood correctly, you mentioned that this was a rapid intervention brigade. Was it under the operation zone staff command?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was under the command of the Drenica Operational Zone command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please mark the area where the 112th Brigade was?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 112th Brigade, now do you want me to mark the command of this brigade, where it was located, or the territory that it covered?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would like you to put an X where the staff was and then mark the area where the brigade was with a circle.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of this brigade was in this area here, between these villages, whereas the area of responsibility of this brigade covered this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put 112 next to the X.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us now about the 113th Brigade, where was its headquarters, and what was its area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of this brigade was based in Ujimire, whereas its area of responsibility -- this was the area of responsibility of this brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, now I would like to ask you to tell us, please do not draw anything on the map, but would you be able to mark the area where the 114th Brigade was on this map or not? If you're unable to do that, we can use a new map so you can mark the area where the 114th was; and if you can, if you're able to mark it on this one, then please go ahead and do it.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we can use the same map because the area of responsibility of this brigade was this one here. This brigade's command was initially based in Gllanasjelle, I'm talking about the period when I toured this brigade, and this is the area of its responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us what -- describe the activities of these brigades in March 1999.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the reports from that time, the task of this brigade was the defence one, to defend the territory and the civilian population in their respective areas of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us in what manner you issued instructions for the population to be defended by the brigades?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In cases of attacks, offensives, that is, all units along the defence axis and the population near the front line or the defence line had to withdraw in the rear so that they would be outside the perimeter of the danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would your order of April 1st, 1999, be a typical order, issuing instructions as to how to act, the order that relates to Belanac [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the case in the majority of cases, this is how the instructions and orders were issued pertaining to the movements of the units and the withdrawal of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you receive reports on the operations in March 1999 within the Drenica Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as we received reports from other operational zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall what these reports were like and what the situation in the field was?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember it, maybe not in details. Based on the reports received from the zones, we received mainly these reports through communication with radio, and satellite phones. It was impossible to receive written reports from the zones. The Drenica Operational Zone as well as the other operational zones during this time-period, 25th, 26th, and onwards when the Serb attacks started, their positions were attacked. The Serb forces advanced to these positions and the movement of the KLA units, their withdrawal, all the reports pertaining to these movements were communicated to us through radio communication and satellite phones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, were you able to communicate with NATO via these satellite phones?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information possessed by the operations centre within the staff and by the part of the operations centre based in Albania on the grouping and the movement of the Serb forces was also conveyed via these satellite phones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi. I think that I saw in one of your statements that you said that while you were in command of the KLA staff that there were about 17 to 18.000 fighters. Was I -- did I see that correctly?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Pursuant to the information I had at the time from the zone commands there were between 17.000 and 18.000 soldiers who performed tasks and duties within the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Of that number, how many men were within the Drenica Operations Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact figure, but I would say approximately 4.000 or 5.000 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00055, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the court usher please put map number D0202426 [as interpreted] on the screen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, could you please help us now. I would now like to have the whole of Pastrik Operational Zone on the map. How far should we zoom it in so that we can see the entire operation zone on the screen, in other words, to cover Suva Reka, Prizren, Dragas, and Orahovac; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now just pull this map up a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
